calling_contract:
Proposed library, not executable software: dataset group instance_relocation supports two independently trained alternatives, contour_push (heuristic boundary_graph) and visual_push (heuristic dual_view_memory). Both are interruptible, closed-loop calls for ONE physical instance and ONE fixed spatial goal, including approach, contact changes, pushing, small corrections and withdrawal. Neither chooses the next letter, a word, or a new staging goal. The High-level Agent (HLA) owns inventory matching, placement/staging goals, ordering, policy selection, cancellation and re-planning. A different instance or spatial goal starts a new invocation; changing observations, contact location or uncertainty does not.
Common caller arguments: scene-versioned instance_id; reference to that instance's current observation-derived foreground template; spatial_goal in the calibrated third-camera undistorted image chart; allowed workspace/obstacle and already-placed-instance references; positional/angular tolerances and maximum call duration. The spatial goal is an explicit image placement: center (u,v) in original 1280x720 pixel coordinates, desired orientation relative to the instance template at invocation, and target foreground silhouette. A pipeline, not the HLA's unaided reasoning, segments/tracks instances and renders the template at the supplied center/orientation. The HLA can instead accept a user-supplied target scene image after instance association. These are IMAGE-space objectives, not claimed metric poses. Large perspective changes require projective rendering from a commissioned tabletop homography; absent that asset the renderer flags its approximation and refuses layouts whose silhouette cannot be realized by a planar rigid piece. No inverse-depth or metric pose oracle is assumed. The image chart, calibration version, reference template, goal and tolerance stay fixed for a call; the current mask/track is updated causally.
For illustration only: after automatic inventory matching, the HLA could request contour_push for scene_12/instance_4, with third-image center (700,420), relative orientation +20 degrees, goal silhouette produced from that instance's template, a proposed 8-pixel/8-degree tolerance, and a 30-second budget. If the edge quality deteriorates but the identity remains trackable in RGB/history, it may cancel and invoke visual_push with the SAME instance and spatial goal, re-expressed against its new invocation template. A word such as CAT alone is not a legal motor-policy call: distinct C, A and T instances, their readable orientation and three non-overlapping spatial goals must first be resolved. Thresholds and selection benefits are hypotheses.
Common observations: original paired third and wrist RGB, q, measured dq, tau_ext, T_base_ee and T_base_flange, timestamps/frame numbers, calibration, validity masks and causal history. Gripper -1/NaN is invalid; it is not evidence of open or closed fingers. No raw depth is required. Policies return a candidate 7-vector of commanded joint velocity plus running/goal_observed/blocked/uncertain/timeout status, track confidence, goal discrepancy, recent discrepancy trend, tool clearance estimate and possible neighbor displacement. Backend interpretation of action_json.dq, joint ordering, rad/s units, update/hold latency, watchdog and limits MUST be verified against the recording controller before any executable command is enabled. Joint_velocity metadata alone is insufficient. Candidate commands are not measured dq and are not integrated as position increments. If required calibration, track, controller verification or fresh observations are absent, return a reasoned unavailable status and request a verified stop, rather than fabricating measurements or zero-filling missing recorded commands.
Proposed execution timing is a verified 20-Hz command interface with latest available 30-Hz observations, explicit image ages and causal buffers. Training preserves every original pairing and timing; duplicated commands at 30 Hz are not independent teleoperation decisions. Do not repair pairings from camera clock differences. The HLA monitors geometric progress and all placed instances; goal_observed is not word success. On stopping, require a new visual stability/readability check and clearance check before the next call. Safety and workspace commissioning, not this dataset, authorize the actual stop and velocity envelopes.
capability_coverage:
Coverage map: contour_push and visual_push both learn initial elevated approach from the two W blocks; within-instance perimeter travel/re-contact and long transport from A-W/A-O/A-L and B-W/B-O/B-L; orientation and alignment corrections from A-L, A-D-align, A-I-align, B-R and B-D-align; inner-boundary engagement from A-D-stage and B-D-stage (wrist views at 4800 and 1800); temporary relocation/staging from A-I-stage1, A-R-stage, A-I-stage2, A-H-stage, A-D-stage, B-I-stage, B-D-stage and B-H-stage; and revisiting a previously moved instance from the separate later R/D/I/H blocks. They are alternatives for the same responsibility, not a serial pair. The graph policy is selected when complete contours and tool projection are reliable; the RGB-history policy is an alternative when local contour extraction is fragmented yet instance identity and goal remain valid. These cues can be computed online. Both retain demonstrated withdrawals, elevated re-positioning and the unusual B-R re-contact/posture motion around 4050-4200 instead of discarding corrections.
User word parsing, open-inventory identity recognition, repeated-character allocation, layout construction, infeasibility detection and sequencing belong to declared auxiliary components plus the HLA; they are not learned as verified capabilities from these recordings. There is no demonstrated grasping, object flipping, disentangling stacked pieces, recovery from a fallen piece, deliberate multi-object pushing, large collision recovery, or arbitrary robot homing policy. There is no separate learned general-purpose free-space planner: the observed approach and withdrawal regimes are internal to either relocation policy, and hazardous travel must cause refusal/re-planning. New-shape pushing is a required hypothesis addressed by the geometry-conditioned designs and explicit tests, not an established capability.
generalization_design:
The task requires unseen letter identities AND unseen physical shapes, new words, new arrangements and new layouts. Do not evaluate only permutations of these seven pieces. Segmentation removes the demonstrated spelling/order as a training condition; each call has an instance and explicit spatial objective. Staging outcomes receive their own goals instead of being mislabeled as progress directly toward the final word. The same conditional motor problem is shared across instances, approaches, straight/curved boundaries, holes, rotations and re-contacts. The contour policy receives current boundary geometry rather than a learned class ID or stored alphabet template; the visual alternative receives an instance-marked scene and explicit goal rather than episode position. These choices address shape and layout variation but two episodes cannot establish broad contact/friction competence.
Semantic generalization is separate: an open-vocabulary visual character/upright-orientation recognizer must map automatically segmented instances to the requested character multiset, including multiple distinct instances for repeated characters. Its weights and evaluation set are not provided. It must output competing hypotheses and reject ambiguous M/W or rotated/symmetric readings, not silently resolve them by the demonstrated word. The HLA matches the multiset, reports impossible inventories without moving, and proposes a baseline, direction, center positions, orientations, spacing and margins in the image chart. It can allocate temporary free areas and re-plan after observed displacements. No fixed WORLD order is embedded. A goal renderer uses the actual observed instance shape; accepting an unknown Unicode character is not evidence that either recognizer or motor policy handles its geometry.
Required independent evaluations: (1) held-out identities and fonts/shapes, with words and positions otherwise controlled; (2) new words and repeated-character requests using familiar shapes; (3) new arrangements, obstructed approaches and non-demonstrated layouts; (4) the joint test of unseen identities, unseen physical shapes AND new words/layouts; (5) impossible inventories and visually ambiguous requests. Shape splits must separate physical exemplars and topology/concavity, not just paint or placements. Measure identification/upright error, instance allocation, per-call position/orientation error, neighbor displacement, contact loss, blocked/uncertain calibration, number of interventions and final word readability/stability separately. Also test illumination, camera occlusion, tool visibility, friction and scale changes, with safety envelopes enforced. Evaluate geometric and visual policies independently, then HLA selection by observable uncertainty; no empirical ranking is asserted.
Only leave-one-episode-out development is possible here, and it is a familiar-inventory/scene test, not the required generalization test. New authorized data with independent shapes/materials, alternate fonts, multiple instances and different goals are needed for the required tests and likely for competence. Proposed ablations (evaluation baselines, not extra callable policies) remove goal conditioning, contour adjacency/normals, object-centered features, history or the target-instance marker. Include a demonstration-order replay baseline to expose accidental task memorization. Large image-plane rotations/translations cannot be treated as physically valid arbitrary new demonstrations without consistent camera/geometry/action conversion. No success claims follow from this plan or artifact validation.
goal_conditioning:
COMMON LABEL RULE G: each segment pins exactly one physical referent and one hindsight achieved placement, not a verified original intention. Its specified goal anchor is the last included paired row, and its goal box is in ORIGINAL third-camera pixels (left,top,right,bottom), before undistortion. Extract only the selected letter foreground from that box, preserving holes and excluding tool/robot; map it through the supplied third Brown-Conrady undistortion with K unchanged. The resulting full-image binary foreground, tight RGB crop, centroid and template-relative orientation are the training-only spatial goal. Identify the foreground by class-agnostic segmentation plus overlap/appearance association to the stated reference; these boxes and visual mnemonics resolve the referent, not a future annotation of which letter/objective to choose. No global word label is assigned. Goal contours/poses are inferred, not verified ground truth.
Current observations are independently segmented and tracked CAUSALLY. Never feed a backward-smoothed current pose or the anchor image as a current observation. Offline bidirectional association may establish which instance a target label refers to, but cannot supply causal current features. Instance selection can be hindsight-labeled while the selected current mask must come from the causal detector. Initialize a new segment's causal tracker from its first available frame with automatic component proposals; associate its episode-local track to the stated referent. If occlusion prevents initialization, early rows have invalid selected-mask features until the track can be established from available history. Use full goal foreground/crop, not just centroid, to disambiguate orientation where possible. Template-to-goal similarity/projective registration supplies orientation and an ambiguity set; ties caused by symmetry stay ties. If the anchor cannot be segmented/associated, or goal registration is inconsistent with a planar rigid piece, suppress condition-dependent loss for that segment and report the derivation failure; do not invent a pose or seek an unspecified internal objective. Determining exact masks is an implementation obligation, not an unresolved choice of goal.
At deployment the HLA chooses an actual scene instance and a spatial placement. The observation pipeline supplies its shape/template, confidence and orientation hypotheses. A deterministic renderer generates the corresponding goal foreground in the same chart from chosen position/orientation; a verified tabletop homography is required when perspective makes a similarity transform inadequate. User metric layouts require that additional commissioned plane calibration; without it accept only valid image-layout requests or report calibration_required. The HLA cannot supply an unmeasured metric object pose by fiat. Upright semantic direction is supplied by the declared recognizer or a user target image; if ambiguous, autonomously pause/report ambiguity, with any optional user clarification explicitly counted as lost autonomy. Goal updates that change the desired placement or selected instance require a new call. Re-contact and clearance changes for the same fixed goal are internal progress, not conditioning switches.
model_inventory:
Available assets: two original paired recordings, RGB/depth references, states/actions and per-episode metadata; third K/distortion/T_base_cam, wrist calibrated K/distortion/T_flange_cam, and TCP xyz [0,0,0.2], rpy [0,0,-90] degrees. Calibration reports 4.420426-pixel reprojection RMS and 3.230258-mm consistency, so fine pose tolerances require uncertainty. The supplied T_base_board is NOT verified to be the tabletop/piece-top plane. Depth scale and RGB registration are unverified and unused.
Shared deterministic components to implement later: exact paired-record loader and validity masks; Brown-Conrady undistortion using the calibration block (not mixing the different wrist factory and calibrated intrinsics); wrist camera pose from T_base_flange*T_flange_cam; tool projection from T_base_ee using the recorded TCP, checked against images before use; timestamp/frame-number freshness features without clock realignment; instance/goal coordinate chart conversion; contour sampling, curvature/normals, signed-distance maps and registration; goal renderer; status/progress and neighbor-motion monitor. Robot/tool image masking requires an automatically detected tool silhouette or a commissioned geometric tool model; TCP location alone does not supply its width. Any model dimensions/robot geometry used for safety must be supplied and validated. No metric inverse projection is needed for the primary image-chart policies. A verified plane homography and tool/table clearance calibration remain commissioning assets for projectively correct/metric layouts and workspace safety.
Shared learned perception, NOT provided: a class-agnostic instance segmentation model with automatic full-scene proposals and calibrated uncertainty, a causal appearance/flow association model, and an open-vocabulary character plus upright-orientation recognizer. Supply licensed/versioned weights and required generic-object/character supervision in a later authorized implementation; these recordings provide neither masks nor a sufficient alphabet-training set. Goal-box hints here are training label anchors, not human clicks required for deployment. Perception must handle unseen shapes using current pixels, not retrieve a known letter mesh/font. Track IDs are arbitrary and episode/scene scoped; IDs never encode spelling. Assignment/registration uses appearance, predicted causal motion and masks; ties, touching objects, lost tracks and visibility gaps are explicit invalid/ambiguous outputs. With no suitable weights these pipelines are not autonomous or runnable; adding per-move human segmentation would violate the intended autonomous operating mode and must not be silently substituted.
HLA support, distinct from motor policies: deterministic word multiset/inventory assignment and geometric layout/clearance feasibility checks; the above recognizer; and a layout renderer. The external HLA selects order and staging locations from current maps, observes changes and chooses the next call. No new learned task planner is claimed or trained from two episodes.
Policy-specific learned components: contour_push has an independently trained variable-size boundary graph encoder, temporal state encoder and 7-command velocity distribution head; optional auxiliary next-observation displacement/contact-affinity heads use only within-segment future targets and are discarded or used predictively online. visual_push has its own independently trained dual-view RGB/goal encoder, causal recurrent/attention state and 7-command velocity distribution head. Frozen generic visual initialization is permitted only if its weights/version and training overlap are disclosed; otherwise train from scratch and expect limited data. They do not share motor weights or ensemble outputs. Both may share the same frozen perception/coordinate conversion assets. Their action supervision is finite action_json.dq, not state dq; missing commands carry zero loss, never fabricated zeros.
Shared action backend, mandatory but unavailable here: recording-controller verification of joint order, units, command hold/update semantics, robot limits, watchdog/stop, singularity and workspace limits. Decode the learned 7-vector directly into that verified joint-velocity interface; do not reconstruct missing commands from v/w or integrate measured dq. v/w/spacemouse and target_pose remain exact source fields for audit; target_pose is not a supplied goal label. No inverse-kinematics, force controller or contact sensor is assumed. tau_ext is a measured residual feature/possible anomaly cue, not calibrated contact force. All perception, converters, monitor, policy networks and decoder must be delivered as executable artifacts later; none is implemented, trained or certified in this stage.
motion_coverage:
All 16,745 original paired rows are materialized once: A=episode_2026091922002701 has 12 intervals partitioning [0,9015); B=episode_2026091922062101 has 10 partitioning [0,7730). There is no fabricated N+1 record. There are 20 inter-instance handoffs in total. At each handoff, 30 rows on either side are retained but excluded from policy action loss because release-versus-next-approach ownership is not exposure-exact; this removes 1,200 possible action-loss rows, not source records. A further per-row validity rule masks null/nonfinite command dq and failed derived inputs. These are not imputed. The 15,545 rows outside the explicit handoff bands are only a maximum candidate supervision count, not a count of independent demonstrations or successful actions.
Inspected broad third-camera views cover both entire recordings; wrist evidence confirms a long slender rigid pushing tool, outer-edge contacts, inner-hole engagement and re-contact. Motion summaries show large initial descent from approximately base z=0.365 m to approximately 0.05 m, mostly low-height planar travel with elevation/withdrawal variations; these coordinates do not prove a surface/contact height. Inspected commands and measured dq are distinct. B around 4050-4200 contains relatively large joint/posture adjustment while the R instance remains the objective; retain it with uncertainty instead of making an unsupported separate recovery label. Recorded endpoints show an arrangement visually consistent with HI and WORLD viewed sideways, but success/request labels are absent and final stability is not certified.
overlap_rationale: No materialized source overlap and no concatenation of unrelated endpoints. Both independent policy alternatives reuse the identical dataset group, which is not additional demonstration evidence. Supervised ranges equal materialized ranges, with the explicitly declared 30-row edge bands excluded from action loss; those rows may be causal context inside their own segment or training-only goal-anchor evidence. There is no cross-segment history window. At invocation/segment start reset motor memory and pad missing history with masks, never borrow future rows or the prior segment's hidden state. At deployment a persistent perception tracker may carry only causal scene identity/state; the selected motor policy is reset and warmed from currently available observations. Memory is not transferred between independently trained policies. Stop/goal anchors can be inside supervision exclusions because they label the preceding objective rather than supplying action targets. Within each policy weight repeated command/frame runs by elapsed robot time and balance segment/instance contributions so long L trials and stationary periods do not dominate. Keep an original source sample in one evaluation partition across all reuses, derived crops, masks and priors. Split by episode at minimum; for new-shape evaluation split by physical instance/shape family as well.
portfolio_rationale: One compatible regrouped motor dataset, two substantive callable alternatives. The evidence repeatedly shows instance-conditioned planar relocation with continuous re-contact, not seven unrelated letter skills. Stage versus final placement, shape, displacement, orientation and tool approach are expressed through observations and the fixed image goal, so separate per-letter/stage networks would waste scarce data. A boundary-graph prior deliberately exposes current shape/topology and contact-side geometry, while a dual-RGB temporal prior retains appearance, local tool cues and occlusion history that a contour bottleneck can discard. They train independently and offer the HLA distinguishable operating regimes, not different seeds or synonyms. Both cover the same demonstrated approach/contact/correction responsibility; neither is mandatory upstream of the other. One generic combined model would hide these differences, but adding separate translation/rotation/approach policies would impose unsupported hard phase boundaries and multiply data scarcity. Separate responsibilities would be justified by future evidence of incompatible tools, lifting or contact modalities, not merely by a different glyph name. Two policies are a design choice, not an empirical optimum.
sharing_and_diversity_audit: Mapping: all a_* and b_* segments -> instance_relocation; boundary_graph -> contour_push; dual_view_memory -> visual_push. Each segment has exactly one fixed selected instance and achieved-placement condition, including distinct staging and revisit calls. A segment boundary is not a policy boundary. Both priors use the same observation/action/source contract after explicit conversion to a common image chart and commanded joint velocities. A graph readout still conditions on absolute robot state/tool projection, avoiding a false claim that arbitrary image rotations leave robot joint actions equivariant. No character one-hot, episode index, visible final word or sequence counter is a motor input. Shared perception errors and controller dependencies are common blind spots; the alternatives are not independent safety redundancy. The graph's proposed advantage is sample-efficient transfer of contact geometry when contours are reliable; the visual model's proposed advantage is retaining cues lost by geometric extraction when RGB identity remains reliable. Both benefits are falsifiable and untested. If the same two pieces always co-occur, instance masking/goal ablations and shape-held-out tests must expose accidental context/word memorization. Do not use random row splits, reused frames or two alternative policies to inflate statistical diversity.

heuristics.action_decoding: Predict the original finite 7-component action_json.dq conditional distribution; execute only its selected current command through the common verified joint_velocity backend. q and measured dq are inputs, not labels. No Jacobian inversion, depth reconstruction or assumed v-to-dq conversion is required. Use verified joint velocity/acceleration/workspace limits and watchdog; if a proposed command violates them, return blocked rather than silently claiming it realizes the goal. Rad/s, joint order and 20-Hz hold semantics remain verification gates; until satisfied outputs are non-executable candidates. Do not command a gripper for this installed pushing tool.
heuristics.applicability: Select for a single flat, separately tracked piece with a usable current contour, visible holes/concavities, trusted tool projection and a valid image goal in the recorded workspace. Especially motivates shape-conditioned transport, reorientation, staging and re-contact. Candidate contour quality, occlusion fraction and registration residual are online selection cues, not hidden contact state. Image/chart or instance ambiguity makes the policy unavailable; no unknown letter class fallback is necessary because it consumes geometry rather than an alphabet ID.
heuristics.augmentation: Use illumination/background/texture variation consistently on current and goal RGB, mask-boundary noise bounded by calibration/segmentation uncertainty, and causal frame dropout with validity masks. Permute boundary-node ordering while preserving adjacency and target/obstacle identity. Translation/rotation of a local coordinate representation is a change of chart: transform ALL contours, tool projections, goal and corresponding coordinate features together, keeping absolute state/readout calibration so the unchanged joint command has the same meaning. Do not rotate a scene crop alone or assign a different desired pose to the same action. Do not warp a familiar shape into an unseen shape and call the old contact motion a valid new-shape demonstration. Hindsight goals are exactly the specified attained anchors, not arbitrary word slots.
heuristics.goal_conditioning: Use common rule G for training. At deployment use the caller's scene-scoped instance and explicit image-chart spatial goal rendered from that instance's currently observed shape, with fixed reference template and symmetry/ambiguity masks. Geometry and goal discrepancies, not W/O/R class names, condition the network. Do not replace the desired shape/rotation with an endpoint-derived online target. A caller change of goal or instance cancels the existing call; automatic contour updates for the same instance are continuous inputs.

handoff.entry_conditions: Verified backend/tool calibration, fresh paired sensors, uniquely selected instance, valid goal and workspace, reliable contour and no unresolved stack/overlap. Initial tool can be elevated or in a safe previously observed low-clearance neighborhood; dangerous unsupported travel is rejected.
handoff.exit_conditions: Return goal_observed only after current target-goal foreground/pose agreement remains within caller tolerances over a proposed 0.5-second causal window and the tool is visibly clear or motion can be stopped safely. Report ambiguous orientation separately. Timeout, loss of track, hazardous approach or caller cancel also terminates; none means success.
handoff.failure_signatures: Large contour/goal registration residual, fragmented or swapped mask, tool projection disagreement, commanded motion with no selected-piece response, unintended neighbor motion, repeated error oscillation, increasing uncertainty, joint limit/safety rejection, or force-residual anomaly. No tau_ext threshold is a ground-truth contact label.
handoff.overlap_role: No cross-segment motor memory. Excluded handoff bands preserve observation context without labeling next-target motion as the old goal; reset graph temporal state at a new invocation. Same-group policy reuse adds no evidence.
handoff.successor_readiness: Return current instance/goal residuals, track validity, tool clearance and a scene version. The HLA must re-check all placements and choose the successor target; this policy never automatically follows the demonstrated order.

heuristics.input_preprocessing: Implement the common loader, validity masks, undistortion, automatic instance segmentation/tracking and tool projection in model_inventory. In the fixed third image chart sample variable-size ordered outer/inner boundary graphs at approximately uniform arc length; preserve holes, attach curvature, local tangent/normal with orientation/visibility confidence, target/other-instance flags, tool-relative vectors, and goal-contour distance features. Include workspace boundary and separate tool/global nodes, full q/measured dq/tau_ext/EE transforms, camera identity/calibration confidence and elapsed-time features. Normalize image coordinates by width/height without treating pixels as meters. Use the last up-to-eight valid causal observations and explicit dt/missing masks; no history crosses a segment. Do not infer a complete occluded contour by looking forward; predicted contours have a distinct validity/confidence channel. Current RGB segmentation and track initialization must work without a human point prompt online.
heuristics.limitations: Two episodes, one tool and similar material/scale. Visible contour is not mass distribution, friction or center of pressure. Inner-hole engagement can jam an unfamiliar concavity. Shape transfer, collision avoidance and tolerances are unvalidated. A geometric bottleneck loses texture and can confuse touching pieces or symmetries. Current image geometry is not verified metric geometry; wide layout/perspective changes need the declared plane asset. Cannot recover a fallen/flipped/stacked piece or invent a feasible inventory. Missing perception/controller assets prevent autonomous deployment.
heuristics.pipeline_implications: Train a boundary-adjacency message-passing encoder with shared local edge/contact-affinity functions and an object/tool/global readout that emits joint commands conditioned on q and goal. Add a temporal state encoder for recent selected-piece response and re-contact. Soft attention to reachable visible contour neighborhoods biases the representation without hard-coding a particular side or object order. A separate global pathway must cover elevated approach and withdrawal, so all retained labels are definable without a later phase-label pass. Auxiliary prediction of the selected object's next observed displacement can be trained only for valid same-segment successors; it is a training target, never an online feature. Contact-affinity supervision, if used, is explicitly a weak proxy from tool-to-contour proximity plus subsequent piece motion, not contact truth. Implement and ship all converters, uncertainty masks, graph builder, decoder and monitor with this policy in the later stage.

policy_contract.caller_arguments: Common instance_id, observation template reference, explicit image placement/foreground goal, workspace/obstacle references, tolerance and budget. Caller controls WHAT instance/placement, when to stop, and when to switch; it does not choose latent boundary attention or individual contact points. No untrained contact-side argument is offered.
policy_contract.input_output_contract: Causal two-view observations and state enter the automatic converter; the graph policy consumes the derived geometry/history plus robot state and fixed goal. Outputs one candidate command dq[7] and shared status/progress fields, including contour completeness, registration ambiguity and contact-affinity uncertainty. Gripper feedback remains invalid. All output units/actuation are subject to the common controller gate.
policy_contract.memory_and_handoff: Maintain only within-call temporal graph state and causal object response. Reset at a new goal/instance or alternative-policy handoff; use available current perception tracks, not another policy's hidden state. Training histories are padded/masked at the original cut boundary.
policy_contract.selection_cues: Prefer testing this alternative when boundary continuity, selected-instance association and projected tool/edge location are reliable, especially for unfamiliar visible shapes. Compare with visual_push when edges are fragmented but RGB/history is informative. This is a proposed selection rule, not an empirical ranking; if identity/goal is ambiguous neither policy is appropriate.
policy_contract.status_and_progress: Return centroid and foreground/rotation residual with ambiguity set, recent trend, geometry confidence, number of re-contact/oscillation events, possible neighbor displacement and blocked/uncertain/goal_observed flags. All use current/past estimates. Numerical safety/success thresholds require validation and cannot be inferred from episode endings.

heuristics.rationale: Observed regularity: the same rod engages straight edges, curved edges, corners and the D hole, and repeatedly changes contact while relocating differently shaped pieces (A4800, A8000; B650, B1800, B5850). Learning problem: infer goal-directed joint commands for a selected current shape, including approach/re-contact, without letter-class-specific trajectories. Inductive bias: local boundary adjacency and object/tool/goal-relative geometry share contact features across shapes while a global robot-state readout preserves executable joint semantics. Implementable mechanism: variable-size boundary graph message passing, temporal response state and a supervised 7-command head, with optional within-segment displacement prediction. Falsifiable expected benefit: improved held-out-shape displacement/orientation control versus the RGB alternative or graph-without-boundary ablation when contours are reliable. This expectation has not been tested.
heuristics.statement: Learn one reusable instance-to-placement policy with local boundary/topology sharing and closed-loop geometry feedback; never choose a spelling sequence or retrieve a known letter motion.

heuristics.action_decoding: Use its own learned 7-component command dq head and the SAME verified direct joint_velocity decoder contract, safety gate and stop/watchdog as contour_push. No blend or ensemble of the two motor outputs. Do not integrate command dq as a pose target; do not substitute state dq or v/w when dq is missing. All command order/units/timing must be verified before execution. No gripper actuation is part of this policy.
heuristics.applicability: Alternative for the same one-instance relocation responsibility when the target is still uniquely identifiable but contours are partially occluded/fragmented, lighting is variable, or the wrist image contains useful near-contact appearance cues. Both camera freshness and causal tracking confidence must be adequate; fully lost identity or an invalid goal is not an excuse to continue blind. Applies to the same observed approach/contact/correction regimes, not an independently demonstrated broader recovery capability.
heuristics.augmentation: Apply consistent photometric changes to target/current/goal appearance; independently model realistic camera exposure differences with calibration-aware color normalization. Use causal view dropout, occlusion masks, frame-repeat/drop simulation and timestamp masks to train declared missing-view behavior; never supply future frames to fill a gap. Dropout must not create labels for sustained blind motion. Preserve selected-instance/goal alignment in crop jitter and propagate coordinates to all masks and goal channels. Do not change word/instance/desired location alone while retaining the action. No arbitrary image rotation with unchanged robot actions or synthetic shape warping is accepted as a physical demonstration.
heuristics.goal_conditioning: Use the same fixed instance and G hindsight spatial goal as the graph alternative. Feed goal foreground and masked RGB target crop in a separate goal stream with absolute image goal coordinates, along with the current target-instance marker. Neither raw episode endpoint frame nor visible word is substituted for a target mask. Online goal images are renderer/user-goal outputs supplied at invocation, not future observations. Changing the requested placement or instance is a new call.

handoff.entry_conditions: Verified backend/workspace; fresh observations; selected identity and goal valid; enough current/past RGB to localize the target or a brief explicitly uncertain occlusion. Contour completeness may be lower than required by contour_push but the policy cannot start from an uninitialized or swapped target track.
handoff.exit_conditions: Same observable goal agreement/stability and clearance criterion as the graph alternative, computed by the shared monitor rather than an unexplained neural done bit. Stop also for timeout, cancel, growing uncertainty, invalid sensors or hazards. Final word verification remains with the HLA.
handoff.failure_signatures: Visual target-marker drift or identity swap, incompatible views, increasing uncertainty under occlusion, error plateau/oscillation, repeated tool motion without target progress, neighbor displacement or command safety rejection. A confident recurrent hidden state is not permission to ignore invalid current observations.
handoff.overlap_role: Use only causal within-segment histories. Explicit edge-band loss exclusions prevent ambiguous release/next-approach labels from driving the visual temporal model. It is an independent same-data alternative, not a continuation trained on the graph policy's hidden state.
handoff.successor_readiness: Expose the same current scene version, instance/goal residual and clearance information. The HLA can stop and re-invoke either policy after fresh association; there is no automatic mode cascade or assumed episode phase.

heuristics.input_preprocessing: Implement all common pairing/validity, camera and automatic target-tracking components. Undistort each view with its own declared calibration; retain third global context plus a selected-instance/tool neighborhood crop and wrist contact crop, with crop-to-original coordinate matrices and validity masks. Proposed policy input resolution: 640x360 global images and up to 384x384 detail crops; this is independent of the inspection preview and must preserve small tool/edge detail through evaluation. Include a target mask/soft marker, goal foreground/crop, absolute chart coordinates, robot q/measured dq/tau_ext/transforms, dt, image ages, visibility and missing-gripper masks. Encode last up-to-fifteen causal paired observations; explicit masks handle repeated frames and segment starts. When masks are fragmented, retain the soft marker/track prediction with uncertainty and use RGB rather than supplying a fictional full contour. Persistent ambiguity returns unavailable.
heuristics.limitations: Appearance can overfit brown pieces, stickers, white background, this camera and this inventory; recurrence may memorize ordering without strict goal/instance tests. Same unprovided perception/recognition/backend dependencies as the graph policy. Temporal inference cannot recover arbitrarily long occlusion or certify contact. It may transfer worse to unseen physical shapes despite accepting novel goals; no ranking is known. No success beyond the recorded near-planar single-tool regime is established.
heuristics.pipeline_implications: Train an independent goal-conditioned two-view spatial encoder plus causal recurrent/attention state and a multimodal 7-command output distribution. Instance markers restrict target attention; global RGB retains other pieces/tool context, while wrist RGB resolves nearby edge/inside-hole appearance. Time/history lets inference distinguish recent progress, withdrawal and re-contact without adding hindsight phase inputs. Teacher-force only past observations/actions already available at that time; if previous action is used online, use the actually issued command, not the demonstrator's unavailable future command. Predict one current command rather than open-loop replay or an unspecified long action chunk. Optional next-observation representation loss stays within each segment and is training-only. Ship its own trained network, input pipeline and decoder/monitor dependencies in the later implementation; no graph motor network is required.

policy_contract.caller_arguments: Identical instance and image-goal interface, tolerance, workspace and budget as contour_push, enabling HLA replacement without an oracle conversion. Caller chooses the responsibility and call lifetime; the model internally chooses approach/contact/re-contact actions, not the next instance or staging destination.
policy_contract.input_output_contract: Causal RGB/state/history and target/goal markers to current command dq[7], status and uncertainty/progress. The goal stream is distinct from live observation. No known-alphabet token, demonstration number, verified contact label or depth metric is required. Return unavailable if mandatory scene identity, goal, calibration or backend verification is missing.
policy_contract.memory_and_handoff: Call-local recurrent memory, reset at goal/instance/policy change. A fresh call may warm up from permitted current causal observations using masks; no hidden state transfer or cross-cut training windows. A perception track may persist with its own uncertainty but supplies no future information.
policy_contract.selection_cues: The HLA may test this alternative when the graph contour is unreliable but one or both RGB views still support stable identity and local tool tracking, or when recent visual response clarifies re-contact. If contour geometry is high-confidence, contour_push offers a more explicit shape bottleneck. Selection and tolerable occlusion duration must be validated; neither is claimed superior.
policy_contract.status_and_progress: Return shared geometric progress with uncertainty plus view consistency, target-marker confidence, temporal innovation and predictive action dispersion. During partial occlusion report degraded observability rather than apparent progress from hidden state alone. Use shared current-observation termination checks and reason-coded blocked/uncertain/timeout.

heuristics.rationale: Observed regularity: the robot/tool occludes the third view while wrist frames expose the local letter boundary; contact approaches, pauses and re-contact can look similar in one still (A4800 versus A5600; B3900,4050,4200). Learning problem: infer the current command from causal visual interaction history and an explicit fixed target instead of requiring a perfect geometric reconstruction. Inductive bias: target-marked dual-view attention plus recurrent response memory. Implementable mechanism: separately encoded global/wrist/goal images, robot-state fusion, causal temporal model and supervised current-command distribution. Falsifiable benefit: less degradation than a contour bottleneck under short partial occlusion/edge fragmentation with stable identity; test also whether this costs unseen-shape transfer. It is a substantive independent callable alternative, not merely a seed or evaluation baseline.
heuristics.statement: Learn an independent two-view temporal visual relocation policy that retains near-contact appearance and causal response history lost by a contour-only representation.

skills.name: Instance-conditioned relocation, staging and alignment
skills.segmentation_rationale: Cuts follow changes of selected physical instance and fixed hindsight placement, not equal duration or a predefined task phase order. All reference letters below are visual mnemonics for specific pieces, not verified semantic labels. A and B prefixes denote their original episodes only. First/last paired records of every cut and images of their first/last supervised rows were inspected; neighborhoods and wrist detail were used for uncertain handoffs. Exact material boundaries select a handoff REGION, not a claimed exact contact-change timestamp. Thirty rows on both sides of each inter-instance boundary are explicitly excluded from action loss, retaining context and goal evidence without inventing exposure-level synchronization. Within each interval the declared instance and goal are fixed; approach, perimeter travel, pressing, contact loss/re-contact, orientation corrections and withdrawal can be produced for that goal without another semantic label pass. Repeated visits to R/D/I/H have different local endpoints and are distinct invocations, even if a human might have had one larger word objective. L's prolonged reorientation and transport is kept together because the inspected evidence supports one continuing selected instance and one hindsight endpoint, not an intervening target switch. Differences are observations/goals in a shared learning problem rather than a reason for one policy per segment.

skills.subgoal: Relocate one caller-selected physical piece to one explicit spatial placement, whether temporary staging or alignment, while retaining the demonstrated approach, contact changes, corrections and withdrawal. The HLA retains all multi-instance and word-level control.

task_interpretation:
The intended autonomous task is to arrange physical letter instances into a currently requested word under explicit layout constraints, including completely unseen identities and physical shapes. These two demonstrations show a Franka-mounted long slender rigid pushing tool moving seven flat brown letter-shaped pieces on a white surface. Third and wrist views support planar pushing, inner/outer-edge engagement, changes of contact, elevation for re-positioning, temporary displacements and revisits. The apparent inventory can be described visually as W/M-like zigzag, annular O-like, R-like, L-shaped, D-like and two differently oriented crossbar pieces (H/I-like). These names are mnemonic associations to visible instances, not provided letter labels. The final images look consistent with HI beside WORLD viewed sideways, but neither a requested word nor success is annotated. In particular, endpoints are not proof of success.
The motor learning unit is not an episode or a letter category: it is a specific instance-to-achieved-placement invocation. Temporary R/D/I/H moves are distinguished from later revisits. Hindsight endpoints provide explicit spatial training conditions, with causal live-state inputs kept separate. Word understanding, inventory feasibility, upright semantic interpretation, layout and sequencing remain explicit upstream responsibilities supported by declared models. No assumption that a new word is merely a rearrangement of the demonstrated alphabet is acceptable. Autonomous deployment still requires perception weights, verified backend/safety semantics and, for metric/projective layouts, additional commissioned geometry assets; these are obligations, not assets claimed present.
unobserved_cases: No recordings establish recognition or manipulation of wholly new letter identities/fonts/topologies, distinct repeated-character instances, new friction/materials, arbitrary metric layout precision, crowded/stacked inventory, flips, falling off the table, picking/grasping, robust multi-object collision recovery, or high-level planning success. No verified force/contact/success labels, object masks/poses, word requests or complete robot-controller execution specification are provided. These gaps do not remove the required unseen-shape/word task: the proposed geometry-conditioned and RGB-history alternatives plus the recognition/layout/HLA pipeline explicitly target it and must undergo the independent tests described above. Competence remains untested and likely needs more authorized diverse demonstrations and evaluation assets. One-time human-assisted safety/camera/table/tool commissioning is a disclosed deployment dependency, not per-move human selection. Optional user clarification of an impossible/ambiguous request must be counted separately from autonomous feasible-task success. All present work stops at cuts, supervision contracts and independent prior/policy designs.
